answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 538 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the jade seed, the ivory timing is verifiable from the copper record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 268 keys as a result forfeits 268 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
